To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) memory virtualization is a promising approach to overcome the memory wall problem in DNN training; and (b) accelerator-centric DL systems can provide a more scalable and efficient platform for training deep neural networks.

(i) memory virtualization is an effective technique for reducing the memory footprint of DNN training, (ii) accelerator-centric DL systems can be used to overcome the memory capacity wall and provide a scalable solution for DNN training.

(1) memory capacity wall is a key bottleneck in designing a scalable HPC system for DL; (2) DNN virtualization is a promising solution for overcoming the memory wall bottleneck; (3) DNN virtualized training is scalable and energy-efficient, but it is limited by the memory capacity wall of the DL accelerator; (4) accelerator-centric DL system is a promising research direction to overcome the memory capacity wall bottleneck.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of scalable, energy-efficient, and programmable accelerator-centric HPC systems for deep learning.
the following three questions: (1) What are the key challenges in designing scalable and energy-efficient DL systems?
the development of a system architecture that is scalable and energy-efficient for training deep learning algorithms.

the future of DL system architecture is accelerator-centric, which will be a key driver for future research on DL system architecture.
the memory capacity bottleneck problem in DL is a major roadblock in the path of designing a scalable HPC system for DL.
the current state-of-the-art DNN memory virtualized system architecture is a promising research direction to design a scalable, energy-efficient, and programmable DL system architecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a scalable and energy efficient DL system architecture can be achieved by combining the following three elements: (1) a scalable and energy-effcient HPC system, (2) an accelerator-centric DL system, and (3) a memory virtualization technique for reducing the memory consumption of the DNN model.
we are proposing a memory virtualization framework for deep learning that enables the study of large-scale deep learning algorithms.

the design of an accelerator-centric DL system architecture is a promising research direction to overcome the memory capacity bottleneck and enable scalable and efficient training of large-scale deep learning models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a system architecture that is designed around the accelerator, and not the other way around, is more suitable for scaling up the memory capacity of the accelerator and hence the size of the DNN that it can train.
a scalable and energyefficient deep learning system architecture will require a system design that is accelerator-centric.
a scalable and energy efficient DL system should be designed around the accelerator, not around the memory.
